title: Internal Admin IT Finance Security Operational Sync
next_steps: Lena to share updated finance allocation spreadsheet (dedicated capacity line items) by 2026-05-18
Avery to propose two 2-hour KMS rotation windows and test plan by 2026-05-20
Samir to draft SOC2 evidence checklist and list outstanding items by 2026-05-17
Maya to run a dry-run incident drill with infra on 2026-05-25 and share notes
action_items: Avery - schedule KMS rotation windows and send calendar invites - due 2026-05-20
Lena - update cost allocation for Dedicated pilot and confirm procurement path - due 2026-05-18
Samir - collect last audit logs and identify missing retention policies - due 2026-05-17
Priya - review updated Master Services Agreement clauses for VPC/on-prem - due 2026-05-22
transcript: 00:00 - Lena Morales: Alright everyone, uh, thanks for joining. Let's give folks another minute to drop in, but we can start — we have a packed agenda: KMS rotation, SOC2 evidence, Dedicated pilot budget alignment, and procurement timing.

00:45 - Avery Chen: Yep, I'm here. Quick note, Diego sent a note earlier about an unexpected quota bump on test cluster that we should account for in the cost spreadsheet, might skew the month-to-month on the Dedicated pool cost estimates.
01:10 - Diego Alvarez: Sorry, yeah that's me. We triggered a scale test yesterday, the billing meter didn't backfill as expected. We'll reconcile but wanted to flag — might look like a spike.

02:05 - Samir Patel: For SOC2, I'm tracking the usual suspects: log retention, privileged access reviews, encryption at rest and in transit, and incident response documentation. I still need the last three months of audit logs from the billing stack.
03:00 - Lena Morales: Right, on billing logs — Priya, do you have the procurement ticket that ties to the reserved GPUs? We need to map cost centers before finance approves the commitment.

03:22 - Priya Rao: I do, I do. It's in JIRA under MS-2247, but Michael updated the PO template last week so I'll attach the revised PO and the clause about data residency to the ticket after this call.
04:05 - Maya Jones: Quick clarifying question — when we say KMS rotation, are we rotating customer-managed keys or our service keys? That changes the outage window and the steps quite a bit.

04:28 - Avery Chen: Good call. This rotation is for our backend service keys that wrap customer keys — so technically it's internal, but we still need to ensure it doesn't break Dedicated instances that have pinning enabled.
05:00 - Samir Patel: Put another way, we need a canary plan. If the rotation touches active KV caches, we could see stale token failures. So schedule a small canary region first.
06:15 - Lena Morales: Finance question — are we comfortable committing to three months of reserved capacity for the pilot, or do we want a shorter commit and extend if usage meets thresholds?
06:40 - Diego Alvarez: From infra ops, three months gives us stable scheduling for GPU procurement and reduces churn, but I get finance pain. Maybe 90-day with a 30-day opt-out clause?
08:05 - Priya Rao: Legal will need clear exit language. If there's an opt-out, define SLAs and termination liabilities. I'll draft language but need the cost delta numbers from Lena.
09:30 - Lena Morales: I'll put two lines in the spreadsheet: committed rate and on-demand fallback, with projected savings and break-even. Will share by next Tuesday.
10:20 - Avery Chen: On the technical side, we should also determine which models are part of the pilot. Some of the larger seq-len tasks change kernel selection and memory use — affects scheduling.
11:00 - Maya Jones: Agreed. I recommend we pick one low-latency chat model and one long-sequence summarization model to cover extremes. I'll assemble a perf matrix.
12:00 - Samir Patel: Back to SOC2 — for evidence, I need confirmation on RBAC reviews. Have teams been doing quarterly role reviews? I'm seeing some stale dev accounts still with privileged roles.
13:10 - Diego Alvarez: We ran a cleanup in March but not a formal quarterly review. I'll trigger a targeted review for the infra and prod clusters and produce a remediation plan.

14:00 - Lena Morales: Also we need to finalize retention policies for billing and usage telemetry. Current default is 90 days for detailed telemetry and 13 months for aggregates; is that still good for audit?
14:30 - Samir Patel: SOC2 asks for documented retention rationale. 90/13 seems fine, we just need screenshots and the policy doc. If anyone has the last policy version, drop it into the audit folder.
15:45 - Priya Rao: I'll upload the updated MSA clause and the data residency appendix after lunch, noted.
17:10 - Lena Morales: On procurement timing — Jared, what's realistic for getting the PO approved once we hand you a final spreadsheet?
17:34 - Jared Kim: If finance has the spreadsheet and approvals, procurement can issue the PO in 5 business days. Legal review of contract addenda might add another week depending on redlines.
18:50 - Maya Jones: Another ops risk: if we change quantization/packaging for the pilot to save costs, we need to flag eval quality regressions. Optimize team should be in the loop.
20:00 - Avery Chen: Good point — Redwood Optimize recommendations should be in the technical runway. Maya, can you coordinate with Optimize and put a short checklist in the pilot runbook?
20:30 - Maya Jones: Yup, I'll add that. Also will include cache warm-up notes to avoid initial latency spikes.
22:15 - Samir Patel: Incident drill — propose a 2-hour runbook dry-run focused on KMS failover and model fallback to hosted variants. We need to verify fallback policies work end-to-end.
23:40 - Diego Alvarez: I'm available 2026-05-25 for the drill. We'll need a few engineers and the SE on call to validate RPCs and KV cache state transitions.

25:00 - Lena Morales: Let's align calendars after the call. Also quick note on cost center attribution for tagging — Diego can you confirm tags are enforced for Dedicated instances so finance can allocate?
25:38 - Diego Alvarez: Tags are partially enforced via policy but not retroactive. I'll run a sweep to tag untagged instances and add a pre-commit hook for new deployments.
27:10 - Priya Rao: Legal question — for VPC/on-prem customers, do we have any default indemnity language that differs? I need to confirm obligations around audit access.
27:55 - Maya Jones: There's a standard appendix we use; I can send the template. But for on-prem we usually remove remote read access clauses and offer local audit bundles.
29:00 - Samir Patel: For the SOC2 evidence, what format do we prefer? Is a shared drive with permalinks okay, or do we need formal artifact uploads to the compliance portal?
29:25 - Priya Rao: We prefer the compliance portal so we can track upload receipts. But short-term, a shared drive with consistent filenames is acceptable as long as we move things within 48 hours.
31:00 - Lena Morales: Anything else on the cost side? I know there's concern about the billing meter artifacts being noisy during scale tests.
31:25 - Diego Alvarez: Yes, note to everyone: mark scale tests in the ops calendar and tag them 'scale-test' so finance can exclude them from monthly forecasting.
33:10 - Avery Chen: Regarding KMS key rotation steps, I'll outline: pre-rotation backup, staggered key activation, canary region, monitor for auth errors, rollback plan. Will share the doc.
34:05 - Samir Patel: When you share, include the metrics we'll monitor: auth failure rate, 5xx errors on inference endpoints, and cache miss rate. We need thresholds for automatic rollback.

35:40 - Maya Jones: For the Dedicated pilot, I ran a quick estimate: if we reserve a 4-GPU cluster for three months, projected savings are ~22% vs on-demand but requires a $X committed spend. I'll put numbers in the sheet.
36:55 - Lena Morales: Please redact exact dollar amounts in meeting notes but attach the spreadsheet to the procurement ticket for reviewers.
38:10 - Priya Rao: One more legal point — ensure MSAs reference our encryption-at-rest defaults and the customer's responsibility section for key management if they opt for BYOK.
39:00 - Diego Alvarez: On-tech note: if a customer opts BYOK, we need to validate KMS access policies during onboarding. That will add ~2 days to onboarding schedule.
40:20 - Samir Patel: I'll add a BYOK checklist to the onboarding runbook and the SOC2 evidence bucket so we can show process controls.

41:55 - Lena Morales: Ok let's do a quick recap of next steps — Lena shares spreadsheet, Avery shares KMS plan, Samir shares evidence checklist, Maya schedules dry run, Priya finalizes legal language.
43:00 - Jared Kim: Procurement will await the spreadsheet and legal sign-off, then issue the PO within 5 business days, we'll aim for the pilot to start the week after next.
44:15 - Diego Alvarez: Small ask — can we add a tag to calendar invites that indicates "no-production-impact" or "production-impact" so teams can plan? That helps prioritization.
45:00 - Maya Jones: Good idea. I'll add a calendar convention to the runbook.
46:35 - Priya Rao: I'll also ask Legal to create a short redline summary when we send contracts for procurement so reviewers aren't re-reading whole docs.
47:50 - Samir Patel: For the SOC2 timeline, we're aiming to have all evidence uploaded two weeks before the auditor's scheduled review; that gives us time for remediation.
49:10 - Lena Morales: Two weeks before — noted. Which dates does that map to for the current audit window? Priya?
49:35 - Priya Rao: Auditor kickoff is 2026-06-15, so evidence in portal by 2026-05-31 ideally.
50:20 - Avery Chen: That compresses our timeline — I'll prioritize the KMS rotation plan and make sure we can show a dry-run pre-05-31.
51:40 - Maya Jones: I'll coordinate engineer availability for the dry-run and share a proposed attendee list in Slack.
52:50 - Lena Morales: Anything else? If not, we'll close with confirmed owners and due dates. Great cross-functional work, thanks everyone.
54:00 - Diego Alvarez: Quick comms note: I'll leave a short postmortem template in the ops channel for the dry-run so we can capture learnings.
55:10 - Priya Rao: I'll schedule a follow-up legal/finance sync next week to go over the redlines and PO sequencing.
56:00 - Lena Morales: Perfect — meeting adjourned. I'll send minutes and the spreadsheet link within 24 hours. Bye everyone.
56:20 - (call ended)
